claims.text: The identity of X is the primary control on whether CrFeCoNiX forms and maintains a protective oxide above 900 °C.
Al or Si additions promote selective oxidation of Cr together with Al or Si.
Al- or Si-containing variants form thin, adherent, slow-growing mixed Cr2O3/Al2O3 or Cr2O3/SiO2 scales.
The Al- or Si-containing oxide scale is chemically and crystallographically coherent with the CrFeCoNiX substrate.
Oxide–substrate coherency relieves interfacial or lattice-misfit stresses.
Mn is a major oxide-forming element in CrMnFeCoNi and produces non-protective oxides accompanied by bulk Mn depletion.
Mn undergoes rapid outward diffusion during oxidation.
Mn forms volatile oxides under the proposed high-temperature exposure.
Mn-containing variants form high-volume or poorly adherent mixed oxides that crack and spall.
Lower oxygen diffusivity and strong oxygen affinity in the Al- or Si-containing variants cause formation of a dense, slow-growing protective scale.
A single-phase solid solution provides a more uniform elemental distribution and consequently promotes a homogeneous, coherent oxide scale.
Multiphase structures create local compositional gradients that can alter oxide adherence.
Interphase boundaries can accelerate local oxidation or act as diffusion barriers depending on their coherency.
At temperatures above 900 °C, Al- and Si-containing variants will have lower weight gain and less spallation than Mn-containing variants.
Mn-containing variants will show rapid oxidation, nonuniform scales, and increased cracking or spallation.
Single-phase variants will form more uniform oxide scales than multiphase variants under identical exposure conditions.
